methodology.driver: httpx.ASGITransport (in-process; no socket, no server process)
methodology.isolation: each repeat runs in its own freshly spawned interpreter with its own application and event loop; nothing is shared between repeats or between frameworks
methodology.ordering: repeats are interleaved round-robin across frameworks and workloads
methodology.lifespan: the lifespan startup handshake is driven for every framework before the first request
methodology.startup_scope: import + build app + first ready request, in a fresh subprocess per repeat
methodology.throughput_definition: completed requests / elapsed wall time of one repeat
methodology.latency_definition: per-request round trip observed by the in-process client, pooled over a repeat
methodology.latency_includes: httpx + ASGITransport client overhead, not handler-only time
methodology.percentile_method: linear interpolation over the request latencies of each repeat
methodology.spread_definition: (max - min) / median * 100, over the per-repeat values of that statistic
methodology.contract_enforced: every repeat re-checks its workload against benches/workloads.py on the application instance it is about to time
methodology.not_measured: memory / RSS is out of scope for this comparison
methodology.caveat: in-process numbers are comparable between frameworks but are NOT a deployed-configuration number (uvicorn/gunicorn/granian over a socket)

not_measured.entrypoint: none — aiohttp.web.Application is not an ASGI application
not_measured.reason: aiohttp.web.Application exposes no ASGI callable: its __call__ is a gunicorn-compatibility stub that takes no arguments and returns self, and the distribution ships no ASGI adapter. The only PyPI shims (aiohttp-asgi, aiohttp-asgi-connector) adapt in the opposite direction — they host an ASGI app on aiohttp's server — so they cannot put an aiohttp app behind ASGITransport. Hand-writing the bridge would measure the bridge, not aiohttp.

not_measured.entrypoint: none — Robyn is a facade over a compiled Rust HTTP server
not_measured.reason: Robyn's Python object configures a compiled Rust server that owns its own socket: the object exposes start()/serve(), defines no __call__, and the package ships no ASGI module (its submodules are router, ws, responses, ... but nothing ASGI). There is no in-process request path to drive, so no comparable number can be produced without measuring Robyn's own server against a socket, which is a different benchmark.
